answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to post a refundable stake before trading, like a lantern hung at the door: one light, one identity, and a bad actor forfeits the bond if caught cheating. An attacker spawning fake copies must fund every one, so flooding the island of honest participants gets expensive fast. Reputation then accrues per stake, not per account, and a newcomer starts on a narrow ledge of low trust until its history proves it. Sybils stop being free.
